key_insight: By combining photoluminescence imaging with drift-diffusion modeling and Bayesian inference, the study maps where and how perovskite solar cells degrade over time.
engineering_relevance: The approach helps engineers identify whether failure originates at the electron or hole transport interfaces, or in the bulk, enabling more targeted durability improvements.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to device physics
Bayesian inference to generate spatial maps of recombination-related parameters during aging
evidence_signal: The method was tested on devices aged under 70 °C full-spectrum sunlight, revealing spatially non-uniform parameter changes and stronger degradation at perovskite/transport-layer interfaces.
watch_item: The inferred maps depend on model assumptions and image quality, so mis-specified physics or noisy measurements could affect how confidently degradation sites are assigned.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
